questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: What the Moon can teach us about early Earth
The life and famous words of astronaut Neil Armstrong
How rockets are built and tested
Why Russia's space programme is failing
questions.why: They discuss the new interest in the Moon, which is really about the origins of Earth.

questions.q: What happened to interest in the Moon after 1969?
options: It grew every year
Many countries sent astronauts there
It stayed the same until 2023
It faded away for decades
questions.why: Georgie says in the decades after that event, interest in returning to the Moon faded away.

questions.q: What happened in the 2023 race to the Moon?
options: Both spacecraft landed safely
Russia's spacecraft landed first, and India's crashed on landing
Russia's craft crashed and India's landed successfully
Neither spacecraft reached the Moon
questions.why: Neil says Russia's rocket crashed, but Chandrayaan-3 successfully touched down.

questions.q: According to one theory, how did the Moon form?
options: It was pulled in from another solar system long ago
Another planet hit Earth and broke off a piece
It grew from comets joining together
It formed at the same time as the Sun
questions.why: Another planet crashed into Earth, breaking off a part which then formed the Moon.

questions.q: Why is the Moon such a good record of the early solar system?
options: It is covered with ice
It is very close to the Sun
Its surface doesn't change and it has no atmosphere
Its surface is always moving and changing, just like Earth's
questions.why: Dr Smethurst says it's inert rock with no atmosphere, so everything is still recorded.

questions.q: What is the far side of the Moon like, according to Dr Becky Smethurst?
options: Smooth and flat
Covered in craters
Full of water
Hidden by thick clouds
questions.why: She says it's incredibly pockmarked, with craters all over it.

questions.q: Where do scientists think Earth's water came from?
options: From the Moon itself
From underground volcanoes
From the other planet that crashed into Earth
From comets and asteroids hitting Earth
questions.why: Dr Smethurst says Earth's water is thought to have come from impacts with comets and asteroids.

questions.q: What does Dr Smethurst suggest finding heavy minerals from comets on the Moon would do?
options: Prove where the Moon's water, and probably Earth's, came from
Show that the Moon is getting smaller
Allow people to live on the Moon
Prove that there was once life on the Moon, billions of years ago
questions.why: She calls it a “smoking gun”: that's where the water came from, and likely Earth's too.
